text: You can't always rely _____ other people to do the work for you.
note: Rely on (or depend on) someone or something.

text: Everyone in the village will benefit _____ the new health centre.
note: Benefit from something. (A benefit of something is the noun: the benefits of exercise.)

text: The new advertising campaign is aimed _____ teenagers.
note: Aim at / be aimed at a group of people or a target.

text: There is a serious lack _____ clean drinking water in the region.
note: A lack of something. The noun is followed by "of" (the verb is not: they lack experience).

text: The minister resigned _____ his position after the scandal.
note: Resign from a job or position. (Without an object: He resigned.)

text: Her skin is very sensitive _____ strong sunlight.
note: Sensitive to something (light, noise, criticism). Sensitive about = easily upset by a topic.

text: We should be more tolerant _____ people who think differently from us.
note: Tolerant of something or someone (also: tolerant towards people).

text: She seemed completely indifferent _____ the results of the election.
note: Indifferent to something = not interested in it.

text: Young children are often fascinated _____ dinosaurs.
note: Fascinated by (or with) something. Adjectives that describe a feeling caused by something often take "by": amazed by, shocked by.

text: Local residents are strongly opposed _____ the plan to build a new road.
note: Opposed to something. (We say "against" with other words: They voted against the plan.)

text: Your comments are not relevant _____ what we are discussing.
note: Relevant to something = connected with it.

text: He was completely unaware _____ the danger he was in.
note: Aware of / unaware of something.

text: Students under 26 are eligible _____ a reduced ticket price.
note: Eligible for something (a benefit, a prize). Eligible to + verb: eligible to vote.

text: After ten years abroad, she yearned _____ her home town.
note: Yearn for something = want it very much (long for).

text: On holiday, I like to indulge _____ a long, lazy breakfast.
note: Indulge in something = allow yourself to enjoy it.

text: My parents insisted _____ paying for the whole meal.
note: Insist on + -ing form (or on something).

text: I congratulated my brother _____ passing his driving test.
note: Congratulate someone on something.

text: The noise from the street prevented us _____ sleeping.
note: Prevent someone from + -ing form.

text: The committee consists _____ twelve members from different countries.
note: Consist of = be made up of. The verb is never used in a continuous tense.

text: He was accused _____ stealing money from the company.
note: Accuse someone of (doing) something. Compare: blame someone for something.

text: The manager blamed the delay _____ bad weather.
note: Blame something on a cause, or blame the cause for something: They blamed the weather for the delay.

text: It is time to dispose _____ these old computers.
note: Dispose of something = get rid of it.

text: All companies must comply _____ the new safety regulations.
note: Comply with a rule, law or request.

text: Elderly people are more susceptible _____ infection in winter.
note: Susceptible to something (an illness, flattery, pressure).

text: Small children are particularly vulnerable _____ abuse.
note: Vulnerable to something harmful.

text: Drivers are legally liable _____ any damage they cause.
note: Liable for something = legally responsible for it. (Liable to + verb = likely to: liable to change.)

text: The crowd was openly hostile _____ the speaker.
note: Hostile to (or towards) someone or something.

text: There is no point in dwelling _____ the past.
note: Dwell on something = keep thinking or talking about it. (Dwell in = live in, formal.)

text: The most senior judge presided _____ the trial.
note: Preside over a meeting, trial or ceremony.

text: The president officially resides _____ the capital, though he often travels.
note: Reside in a city or country (formal for "live").

text: Your age is irrelevant _____ whether you get the job.
note: Irrelevant to something.

text: The region is renowned _____ its excellent wines.
note: Renowned (or famous, known) for something. "As" is used for a role: renowned as a chef.

text: Children under five are exempt _____ the charge.
note: Exempt from something = free from a rule or payment.

text: The company specialises _____ medical equipment for hospitals.
note: Specialise in something.

text: The refugees had been deprived _____ their basic rights.
note: Deprive someone of something.

text: The film is based _____ a true story.
note: Be based on something.

text: A quiet room is more conducive _____ studying than a noisy cafe.
note: Conducive to something = helping it to happen.

text: The scandal eventually resulted _____ the minister's resignation.
note: Result in = cause. Result from = be caused by: His resignation resulted from the scandal.

text: Employees are entitled _____ four weeks' paid holiday a year.
note: Entitled to something.

text: She derives great pleasure _____ working in her garden.
note: Derive something from something.

text: You must adhere _____ the rules of the competition.
note: Adhere to a rule, plan or principle.

text: It is hard to reconcile his generous words _____ his selfish actions.
note: Reconcile one thing with another.

text: After weeks of pressure, she finally succumbed _____ temptation.
note: Succumb to something (temptation, pressure, an illness).

text: He seems quite incapable _____ telling the truth.
note: Capable of / incapable of (doing) something.

text: The low-lying fields are prone _____ flooding in spring.
note: Prone to something (usually bad) = likely to have or suffer it.

text: The report was bereft _____ any new ideas.
note: Bereft of something = completely without it (formal).

text: His speech was replete _____ references to ancient history.
note: Replete with something = full of it (formal).

text: She grew up in a family steeped _____ the traditions of the theatre.
note: Steeped in history or tradition = full of it, deeply influenced by it.

text: The government is answerable _____ parliament for its decisions.
note: Answerable to someone for something.

text: The prime minister seemed impervious _____ criticism.
note: Impervious to something = not affected by it.

text: After years in the Arctic, he was inured _____ the cold.
note: Inured to something unpleasant = used to it so it no longer affects you.

text: The collapse of the bridge was attributable _____ poor maintenance.
note: Attributable to a cause. Compare: attribute something to a cause.

text: His public statements are at odds _____ his private views.
note: At odds with something = in conflict with it.

text: She has harboured a grudge _____ her former boss ever since.
note: A grudge against someone.

text: He has a deep aversion _____ crowds.
note: An aversion to something = a strong dislike of it.

text: The sale is contingent _____ approval from the board.
note: Contingent on (or upon) something = depending on it.

text: At the age of twenty, she embarked _____ a career in journalism.
note: Embark on something new (a journey, a career, a project).

text: He was bent _____ revenge and would not listen to anyone.
note: Be bent on (doing) something = be determined to.

text: The whole theory is predicated _____ the assumption that prices will keep rising.
note: Be predicated on (or upon) something = be based on it.

text: The students showed an insatiable appetite _____ knowledge.
note: An appetite for something = a strong wish for it.

text: She took umbrage _____ the remark and left the room.
note: Take umbrage at something = be offended by it.
